grades.quote: The new thread will have its own favorite memory locations, which are likely to be quite different. The cache memory will initially suffer many misses, slowing the processor to the speed of the main memory
grades.reason: Explains the throughput-cost half of the question: switching threads makes the cache cold, so many misses slow the processor to main-memory speed. It does not discuss the response-time benefit of frequent switching.
Discusses lock contention and parallelism in xv6. It says nothing about the response-time versus throughput tradeoff of frequent context switches.

grades.quote: typically, most of the computer user’s goals are not expressed in terms of deadlines, but rather in terms of a desire for quick response to interaction and efficient (high throughput) processing of major, long-running computations.
grades.reason: Describes time slices and the goals of quick interactive response and high throughput. It also shows that switching quickly to an I/O-bound thread helps responsiveness. It does not explain why frequent switching reduces throughput.
Exploration project prompts about experiments and measuring context-switch frequency. It gives no explanation of the tradeoff.
